1 By way of present appeal, challenge has been laid to an award dated 01.12.2001 0 passed by the learned Reference Court- Court cum-Addl.
Addl.
District Judge, Gurdaspur

. 
2. Briefly stating, in the present case, some land owned by the appellants appellant situated in the revenue estate of Village Tharra Jhikla Teeka Doong, Tehsil Dhar Kalan, Pathankot (erstwhile hile district Gurdaspur) came to be acquired vide notifications dated 23.06.1995 and 24.11.1995 issued under Sections 4 and 6 respectively of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').
The acquisition was carried out for public purpose, namely, for Hydel Channel of Shahpurkandi Dam Project Project..

At the time of acquisition, certain construction was already existing over the land in question regarding which award was passed by Land Acquisition Collector (for short 'the LAC') on 12.03.1998 granting compensation to the tune of Rs.2,65,020 2,65,020/- to the landowner(s).
Being aggrieved thereof,, the appellant appellants-landowners sought reference under Section 18 of the Act which came to be dismissed.
Aggrieved of the decision dated 01.12.20 .2001, the present appeal has been preferred.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant appellants submits that by way of evidence in the shape of deposition of AW AW-2 namely, Ved Parkash Saini,, approved valuer (possessing Diploma of Civil Engineering), site plan, valuation and assessment report regarding the construction existing over the acquired land were proved on record as Exs. A-1 A RFA-3993 3993-2002 (O&M) [3] and A-2 respectively whereby, the total value of the building was assessed at Rs.4,04,000/-
Rs. and thus, the appellant appellants-landowners were entitled for the same benefit.

b 4. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondents submits that a well-reasoned well reasoned award was passed by the learned Reference Court upon appreciation of evidence available on record and the same thus, calls for no interference an
and d the present appeal needs to be dismissed.

5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the paper-book.
paper book.
I find substance in the submissions made on behalf of the appellants-landowners.
appellant 6.

As per the records, the appellant appellants-landowners were awarded sum of Rs.2,54,530/-

7. On the other hand, the valuat valuation ion of the super structure has been proved on record as Rs.
Rs.4,04,000/- by the appellants- appellant landowner through deposition of AW landowners AW-2/Ved Parkash Saini;; the RFA-3993 3993-2002 (O&M) [4] approved valuer (possessing Diploma of Civil Engineering)
through Site plan (Ex.A-1) (Ex.A and Valuation Report ((Ex.A-2).
8.

Despite a lengthy cross cross-examination examination of AW-2, AW respondents have not been able to impeach the credibility of his deposition, thus, in such circumstances, the Assessment Report (Ex.A-2)) needs to be relied upon as a relevant and substantive piece of evidence for the purpose of determination of compensation in favour of appellants-landowners.

Under similar circumstances, this Court in "Union "Union of India and Ors. Vs. Rattan Chand and Anr."

reported as 2012(1) RCR(Civil), 192 went on to take average of both oth the valuations made by the respective parties.

Adopting the same, in order to balance the equities, the appellant appellants-landowners are held entitled for award of compensation on the basis of average of the two valuations i.e. one made by the LAC @ Rs.
Rs.2,54,530/- and the other one which has been proved on record by the appellant appellants-landowner landowners through the expert valuer (AW-2) (AW ) @ Rs.
Rs.4,04,000/- which comes to Rs.3,29,265 3,29,265/- [(Rs.4,04,000+ Rs.2,54,530 Rs.2,54,530)/2]
alongwith all other statutory benefits.
9. In view of the aforesaid, the present appeal is disposed of.
